newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Menem advised not to meet Moon.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Menem advised not to meet Moon.

text.p: The Argentine government's head of religious affairs tried to discourage President Carlos Menem on Thursday from attending a magazine launch by South Korean evangelist Sun Myung Moon this weekend.

Guests for the Buenos Aires launch of the Spanish-language magazine Tiempos del Mundo on Saturday include former U.S. President George Bush and former Peruvian President Francisco Morales Bermudez. Bush will stay at Menem's Olivos residence.

Argentine Secretary for Religious Affairs Angel Centeno told reporters Menem would make up his own mind about whether to attend the launch of the magazine. But Centeno said he considered Moon's Church of Unification "anti-Christian and blasphemous, with activities close to what is normally known as a sect. Various publications here and abroad call the Church of Unification a destructive sect."

The 76-year-old South Korean evangelist is believed by his followers to be an incarnation of God fulfilling the mission of Christ. Critics say he brainwashes vulnerable people into joining the church. Some countries, such as Germany, consider him a threat to public order and refuse him an entry visa.
During the 1980s Moon served 11 months in prison in the United States for tax evasion. His church's assets span the world and include the Washington Times newspaper.

In Argentina, Moon is buying up land in Corrientes province, where he enjoys the fishing and plans to construct what his followers call "ideal cities." In neighbouring Uruguay he already owns a major newspaper, a hotel and a bank.
"Reverend Moon always comes associated with a series of companies and under the cover of religion can come things like this journalistic enterprise," Centeno said.
Menem received Moon in secret last year, while Bush has had a long relationship with the South Korean evangelist, who is a hardline anti-communist.
